title: Longhouse Diorama
details: 📅 Q3 · Unit 6 · North America and the Caribbean

badge.name: Courtesy Ribbon
badge.line: Only VR curators earn this one. You used a people's real name and told their story with care.

hook.look: A work order is a note that tells museum workers what job to do next.
hook.head: Work Order 17 · Longhouse Diorama
hook.alt: Inside a long wooden house with a curved roof, beds along both walls and a walkway down the middle
hook.cap: Inside a Seneca longhouse built again at Ganondagan, New York (2018). The Seneca are a Haudenosaunee nation.
hook.note: Our museum is making a diorama of a longhouse. Please visit one and tell me about it!

opti.brief: Welcome, curators. Our museum is building a diorama of a Haudenosaunee longhouse. Visit one in VR, then record a short video for me.
opti.collections: No headset today? Come to the collections room. Put each museum card on the timeline. Then tell me what you found.

voice.brief: Welcome, curators. Our museum is building a diorama of a Haudenosaunee longhouse. Visit one in VR, then record a short video for me.
voice.step1: Before your headset, look at how a longhouse is built. Then press Practice and say your two sentences before the timer ends.
voice.step2: Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Longhouse in the filter box, click Iroquois Longhouse, then click Begin Solo.
voice.step3: Move with the thumbstick. Look at the walls and the roof. Find one spot where you can see a lot of the longhouse.
voice.step4: Open Library, then Camera. Click Record video and say your two sentences. Click again to stop. Then send it on the Canvas tab.
voice.step5: Press the Meta button and click Quit. Then open the Canvas assignment and check that your video is there.
voice.extra: Have more time? Turn slowly while you record, so I can see both ends of the longhouse.
voice.collections: No headset today? Come to the collections room. Put each museum card on the timeline. Then tell me what you found.

vr.look: A diorama is a small, real-looking scene of a place. A longhouse is a long wooden home. Many Haudenosaunee families lived in one longhouse together.

place.alt: A tall frame of wooden poles shaped like a long house with a rounded roof, standing in a grassy field
place.html: How a longhouse is built: a frame of wooden poles, covered with tree bark.
place.cap: A longhouse frame at Ganondagan, New York, 1997.

say: This is a Haudenosaunee longhouse, and I see ___.

steps.title: Get ready
steps.html:
@PLACE@

In your video, you say these 2 sentences:

@SAY@

Practice now. Say both before the timer ends.

@TIMER@

This is also in VR: open your menu, click the Canvas tab, then pick our assignment.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Longhouse in Filter environments. Click Iroquois Longhouse, then Begin Solo. (Iroquois is another name for the Haudenosaunee.)

steps.title: Scout the longhouse
steps.html: Move with the thumbstick. Look at the walls and the roof. Find one spot where you can see a lot of the longhouse.

steps.title: Record your video and send it
steps.html:
Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Move the tablet until the longhouse fits.

Click Record video. Say your 2 sentences. Click it again to stop.

Click the Canvas tab and pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your video, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 Want to fix it? Record a new video and send it again.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your video is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? Open Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: Turn slowly as you record, so Opti sees both ends of the longhouse.

vr.full: One video, 30 seconds or less, that shows the longhouse while you say both sentences.

studio.title: Who was here first?
studio.look: A timeline shows things in the order they happened. Older times are on the left. Each museum card shows a group of people from our lesson.
studio.do: Read the date on the card. Tap its spot on the timeline, or drag the card there.

game.miss: Not that spot. Read the date on the card, then find it on the timeline.
game.done: Your timeline is full. Of these 5 groups, the Haudenosaunee and the Maya were here first.

cards.name: Spanish settlers
cards.alt: An old stone church with a bell tower and a carved doorway
cards.ok: Yes! Spanish settlers came starting in the late 1400s.

cards.name: The Haudenosaunee
cards.alt: Inside a long wooden house with beds along both walls
cards.ok: Yes! The Haudenosaunee have lived here for over 1,000 years.

cards.name: French settlers
cards.alt: An old stone square with tall stone houses in Quebec City
cards.ok: Yes! French settlers came in the 1600s.

cards.name: The Maya
cards.alt: A tall stone pyramid with steps on each side and a temple on top
cards.ok: Yes! The Maya built stone cities over 1,000 years ago.

cards.name: African peoples
cards.what: They kept their music and stories alive.
cards.alt: Many carved wooden drums with drum heads on top
cards.ok: Yes. African peoples were brought here starting in the 1500s. Most came against their will.
